chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Abu Jamilyah from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding His Exalted Saying, 'And direct your faces toward every mosque,' he said, 'New mosques, so they were commanded to direct their faces toward the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque.'
Al-Tatari from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about His Exalted Saying, 'And We did not make the qibla which you were upon except that We might make evident who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels.' He commanded him with it. He said: 'Yes, indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was turning his face in the sky, so Allah, Exalted and Majestic, knew what was in his heart, so He said, "We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you toward a qibla with which you will be pleased."'

key_terms.يُقَلِّبُ وَجْهَهُ: Turning his face (in anticipation of revelation)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of facing every mosque in the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration elucidates the transition of the qibla, clarifying that 'facing every mosque' implies orienting towards the Kaaba within the Sacred Mosque, while the Prophet’s interim heavenly gaze served as a divine test to distinguish true followers from those who would revert. It highlights the theological significance of the qibla change as a mechanism for verifying loyalty to the Prophet and establishing the final direction of worship.
